activity_context.topic_title: Cauchy-Euler Equations: Characteristic Equations With Distinct Real Roots

examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation
examples.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
x^2 y'' +2 xy' -6 y= 0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=\dfrac{c_1}{x^3}+ c_2x^{2},
$$

find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
x^2 y'' +2 xy' -6 y= 0, \quad y(1)= 0,  \quad y'(1) = 5, \quad x \gt 0.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We find the constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=0.$ Substituting $y(1)= 0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0 = c_1+c_2 \quad \Rightarrow \quad  c_2 = -c_1.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition $y'(1) = 5.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-3\frac{{c}_{1}}{{x}^{4}}+2{c}_{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y'(1)=5$ and $c_2=-c_1$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =-3{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2} \\ 5 & =-3{c}_{1}+2(-{c}_{1}) \\ 5 & =-5{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{1} & =-1\,⇒\,{c}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{x^3}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-2y=0,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}-2{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }-2{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-2] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2 & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda +1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =2$ and $\lambda =-1.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{2}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-1}.
$$
